newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade ready for Ex-Yugo archives division talks.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade ready for Ex-Yugo archives division talks.

text.p: The Yugoslav government is prepared to hold a meeting on the division of archives of former Yugoslav republics in Belgrade in early September, Tanjug news agency reported on Friday.

"The federal government commission...has supported the Yugoslav side's initiative for a meeting of directors of national archives of newly emerged states of former Yugoslavia and the director of the archives of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia," it quoted an information ministry statement as saying.
The five successor states are Yugoslavia (comprising Serbia and Montenegro), Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia, Macedonia.

Defining state property, access to archives and the final distribution were key issues on which the five parties held opposing views, according to Sir Arthur Watts, the chief international mediator in the ex-Yugoslavia succession talks.
Yugoslavia said in May that it saw room for partial talks in certain areas of the succession negotiations such as issues related to division of archives.
Watts, who toured former Yugoslav states earlier this month, expected the next round of bilateral talks by mid-September and a plenary meeting in early October.
